# Hale

> Hale is a general-purpose programming language with one structural
> construct, the locus, that holds its shape at every scale: a value, a component, a
> service, an application, a fleet of running binaries. Going down, a locus
> contains loci; going up, loci compose into an application, and the recursion
> continues past the process boundary into a deployment plan built from the same
> parts. Wherever a scale closes, the compiler certifies it: effect classes and
> budgets at a function, named claims over an assembled application, one
> constitution proven in every environment that adopts it, and cross-binary law
> over a signed fleet. Memory safety comes from the structure rather than a
> garbage collector or a borrow checker. A locus owns a region, freed wholesale
> when it dissolves. The surface (ASCII-only, names not symbols, explicit
> commitments, a small pattern catalog) reads and writes fluently for humans and
> LLMs alike.

## Start here

- [The model](https://hale-lang.org/model): the structure, and why one shape holds at every scale.
- [Proof](https://hale-lang.org/proof): what the compiler certifies, and the witness it returns.
- [The guide](https://hale-lang.org/docs): a level-by-level tour, from scripts to systems.
- [Install](https://hale-lang.org/docs/getting-started/install): get the toolchain.

## For agents and LLMs

- [Tooling](https://hale-lang.org/tooling): LSP, MCP server, context packs, machine-readable docs.
- [Context pack](https://hale-lang.org/hale-context.txt): single-file spec + styleguide + gotchas, tuned for context windows.
- [llms-full.txt](https://hale-lang.org/llms-full.txt): the concatenated documentation corpus.

## Ecosystem

- [pond packages](https://hale-lang.org/packages): the "non-std stdlib".
- [Playground](https://hale-lang.org/playground): edit, check, run in the browser.
